CEED Strategic Reading According to an article by Pablo R. Suanzes, Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a trilateral meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, potentially alongside the APEC summit in Shenzhen on November 18–19. Citing The Wall Street Journal, the article says the proposed meeting could focus on Ukraine and broader international issues and compares the idea to a modern-day Yalta Conference involving major powers and their spheres of influence. Neither Washington nor Beijing has accepted the proposal, and Kremlin spokesman Dmitri Peskov said there is not yet a clear understanding of whether the meeting will take place or what its agenda would be. The article portrays Moscow as increasingly confident following several recent developments involving U.S.-Russia relations, while describing growing concern in Kyiv about Washington’s approach to the war. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine remains prepared to work constructively toward peace while emphasizing that much depends on the position of the United States.
